title: First trumpet at Phoenix Indian School and his side-of-the-mouth embouchure
summary: He first took up the trumpet in 1923; it slipped to one side of his mouth, and teachers later told him to leave it that way.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Did you start studying any of the instruments like the trumpet or the cornet or French horn before you left Arizona?

Yes, when I went to the Phoenix Indian School in 1923. That's where I first picked up the trumpet. And, incidentally, when I picked up the trumpet, it always slipped to one side of my embouchure. And that's how I happen to this day play on the side of my mouth.

Yea! And when, when now -- I've gone to teachers that have -- different musicians have told me and said why don't you go to a teacher and correct that up there. So I go to the teacher, and the teacher looks at me, and he asks

me to play something. So the teacher's found -- a few of the teachers when I went to take lessons to correct that -- put it in the center of my mouth -- blow in the center of my mouth. They would tell me stay there; it sounds better on that side. So I never got to changing my embouchure.
